newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains cattle market slow at $70 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains cattle market slow at $70 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trade was slow near midday Friday, with most of this week's sales occuring during Thursday's brief but active afternoon activity, feedlot sources said.

About 200 head sold early Friday at $70.00 per cwt in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area and about 800 in Kansas, according to USDA and private sources. The sales were steady with Thursday's price and the bulk of trading this week.
Shipment dates for the cattle sold Thursday ranged the gamut, from a few days to the normal seven-day pick up time frame, sources said.
As of mid-morning Friday, the Panhandle week-to-date sales figure was 69,900 head, including 12,200 formulated and 1,700 contracted cattle for shipment this week, USDA said.
Week to date sales in Kansas for the same period totaled 66,800 head, including 14,100 or about 21 percent contracted or formulated cattle for shipment this week, USDA said.

Feedlot cattle prices this week were underpinned by moderate beef demand, although packers had to discount prices to spark sales, sources said. However, prices rebounded slightly at midday Friday. Beef was quoted up $0.78 to unchanged on 170 fabricated loads sold, USDA said.
